issues.description: The solution implementation of assembleBookstore has a parameter (private static func assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore) while the template (commented stub) and the call in Client.main() expect a parameterless function assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore. This mismatch causes the solution's Client.main() call to not match the method signature, producing a compile-time error and confusing students about the intended function signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's assembleBookstore signature match the template and usage by removing the unnecessary parameter. Change the definition to: private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore { ... } so Client.main() can call assembleBookstore() without arguments. Alternatively, update the call in main to provide the required Bool argument, but removing the parameter is preferable to match the exercise template and instructions.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect an assembleBookstore() function with no parameters, but the solution implements assembleBookstore(check: Bool) -> Bookstore (adds a 'check' parameter). This changes the expected usage/signature of the same conceptual entity and can confuse students about how to call or implement the function.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template by changing the solution function signature to private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore (no parameters). Alternatively, if a parameter is required, give it a default value (e.g. check: Bool = true) so assembleBookstore() can still be called without arguments and matches the expected usage.
